candidate.answerReason: Taking k as the hypotenuse gives k²=289 and k=17. Taking 15 as the hypotenuse gives k²=161, strictly between 12² and 13², so it yields no integer k. The side 8 cannot be the hypotenuse.

methods.label: Consider the possible hypotenuses
methods.explanation: If \(k\) is the hypotenuse, then \(k^2=64+225=289\), so \(k=17\). If 15 is the hypotenuse, then \(k^2=225-64=161\), which is not a perfect square, so this case is invalid. The side of length 8 cannot be the hypotenuse. Therefore, \(k=17\).
methods.levelReason: Finding a side of a given right triangle uses the grade 8 Pythagorean theorem. Square-root extraction and comparison with consecutive squares are grade 7 knowledge.
